xep.header:
Bookmarks hierarchy This specification provides a way to organise bookmarks. &LEGALNOTICE; xxxx ProtoXEP Standards Track Standards Council
XMPP Core XEP-0060 XEP-0402 Etc.
NOT_YET_ASSIGNED &nicoco; &edhelas;
0.0.1 2026-10-17 nc
First draft.

section1.p: This specification provides a way to organise conversations in directories and to order them. This can be used as a private, user-specific organisation of chats, or as the server-provided organisation of a give &xep0503; node.

section2.p: Pubsub nodes supporting the protocol defined in this document include an item with an id of urn:xmpp:bookmarks-hierarchy:0. It has an unique child, the directories element, which has one or multiple children directory elements. These children have two attributes: a unique identifier defined by the id attribute (an opaque string), and a human-readable title attribute. These children are ordered; this defines the order in which these directories SHOULD be displayed to the user.
section2.example: <item id='urn:xmpp:bookmarks-hierarchy:0'> <directories xmlns='urn:xmpp:bookmarks-hierarchy:0'> <directory title="Fun stuff" id="xxx-xxx-xxxx" /> <directory title="Boring stuff" id="yyy-yyy-yyyy" /> </directories> </item>

section2.p: Bookmark items that are part of the same node SHOULD have a hierarchy &xep0402; bookmark extension.

It MUST have a weight attribute which value is a decimal number. They are sorted by ascending weights. Using decimal numbers makes it possible to re-order a single item without modifying the other ones.
The hierarchy element has an OPTIONAL directory-id attribute which value points to the unique ID of a directory defined in the item defined in the previous section.

section1.p: It is possible to use this specification for ordering without organising in directories. In this case, the directories item is omitted and only weights matter.
In the presence of directories, bookmarks are first ordered by directory, and then by weight.

Entities supporting this protocol MUST ensure the consistency of the directories identified in the hierarchy element vs the directories element. For instance, a directory-id MUST not point to an inexisting id in the directories item.
To avoid transient inconsistencies, deleting a directory MUST be preceded by erasing the corresponding directory-ids referring to it.

section1.code:
<?xml version='1.0' encoding='UTF-8'?> <xs:schema xmlns:xs='http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema' targetNamespace='urn:xmpp:bookmarks-hierarchy:0' xmlns='urn:xmpp:bookmarks-hierarchy:0' elementFormDefault='qualified'>
<xs:element name='directories'> <xs:complexType> <xs:sequence> <xs:element name='directory' minOccurs='1' maxOccurs='unbounded'> <xs:complexType> <xs:attribute name='id' type='xs:string' use='required'/> <xs:attribute name='title' type='xs:string' use='required'/> </xs:complexType> </xs:element> </xs:sequence> </xs:complexType> </xs:element>
<!-- Extension carried by a bookmark item. --> <xs:element name='hierarchy'> <xs:complexType> <xs:attribute name='weight' type='xs:decimal' use='required'/> <xs:attribute name='directory-id' type='xs:string' use='optional'/> </xs:complexType> </xs:element> </xs:schema>
